skill: Use product and power logarithm rules to expand or combine two factors; on hard items substitute known logarithms into the resulting weighted sum.
reasoning_steps: Identify the common logarithm base and multiplicative factors.
Apply log_b(x^m y^n)=m log_b(x)+n log_b(y), or its reverse for combining.
For hard numeric/symbolic givens, substitute each supplied logarithm into its corresponding coefficient and simplify.
Select the equivalent expression or value from five radio choices.
response_contract: All four bank items have one selection radio field with five math choices. Canonical example has no captured answer field. Hard source questions have complete keys and worked solutions; the two other bank questions lack captured keys/solutions, whose answers can be independently derived.
difficulty: Requested hard is grounded in q-79453 and q-98925: expansion followed by substitution and short arithmetic; q-98925 retains one symbolic parameter.
invariants: Common valid logarithm base; positive arguments.
Product and power rules only; no quotient rule required even though the wider lesson teaches it.
Two multiplicative factors or two additive logarithm terms; comparable short workload.
Five radio alternatives, exactly one mathematically correct choice.
permitted_variations: Base, positive known log values, exponents, variable letters, and option ordering.
The symbolic given may belong to either factor; its exponent may change. The numeric given need not always be the second factor.
Both exponents and their assignments to known values may vary, including unit exponents where instructional workload is preserved.
Complete misconception banks should vary with parameters and remain distinct. Combining/expansion source families remain reproducible, although only the substitution families have explicit hard tags.
essential_vs_incidental: The mapping of each factor exponent to its own given logarithm is essential. The source bases 5/2, letters x/y/k, exponent assignments 2/3 or 1/3, which factor has the symbolic given, and answer positions are incidental. A correct weighted sum is the intended skill, whereas guessing a fixed position or recognizing a uniquely formatted choice bypasses it.
